# UE5 contract error model

**Contract:** `1.0.0-candidate.1` · **Status:** PROPOSED

Generated from `packages/contracts/src/ue5/`. A drift test fails if this file and the
source disagree, so what follows is what the code actually enforces rather than what a
document once said it would.

## The rule the rest of this depends on

> **The HTTP status says whether the batch was processed. It never says whether the
> events were accepted.**

`200` means the batch was processed — read the per-event results, even when every event
in it was rejected. Any non-2xx means nothing was stored and the whole batch is safe to
resend unchanged.

## Request level

| Code | HTTP | Meaning | Retryable | Outbox | Sending | Operator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `malformed_request` | 400 | The batch envelope could not be parsed, or carried a forbidden field. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | no |
| `unauthorised` | 401 | The credential is unknown, malformed, revoked or superseded. | no | `retain` | `stop` | yes |
| `source_suspended` | 403 | The credential is valid; the source is suspended or archived. | no | `retain` | `stop` | yes |
| `batch_too_large` | 413 | Over the batch event count or byte ceiling in force. | yes | `retain_and_split` | `continue` | no |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Too many requests. Retry-After states how long to wait. | yes | `retain` | `backoff` | no |
| `unavailable` | 503 | The backend could not process the request. | yes | `retain` | `backoff` | no |

## Event level

| Code | Meaning | Retryable | Outbox | Sending | Operator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `malformed_event` | The event envelope is unparseable, or a required envelope field is missing. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | no |
| `schema_unknown` | This event name is not registered at this schema version. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | yes |
| `schema_invalid` | Properties do not satisfy the registered contract for this event. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | no |
| `unsupported_version` | The schema version is outside the range the server accepts. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | yes |
| `event_too_large` | The serialised event exceeds the per-event ceiling. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | no |
| `reserved_property` | A property key is reserved: identity, server-assigned, or the observer namespace. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | no |
| `clock_out_of_range` | occurred_at falls outside the acceptance window in force. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | yes |
| `pii_suspected` | A property matched a forbidden-content heuristic. | no | `quarantine` | `continue` | yes |
| `storage_error` | A transient failure while writing this event. | yes | `retain` | `continue` | no |

## Codes this build has never heard of

| Situation | Retryable | Outbox | Sending |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unrecognised **event** rejection code | no | `quarantine` | `continue` |
| Unrecognised **4xx** | no | `quarantine` | `continue` |
| Unrecognised other status | yes | `retain` | `backoff` |
| No response at all (timeout, reset, lost acknowledgement) | yes | `retain` | `backoff` |

An unrecognised event code is treated as non-retryable **whatever the server said about**
**`retryable`**. A client that retries something it cannot interpret retries for ever, and
a quarantined event an operator can see is a better failure than an infinite loop nobody
notices.

## Rationale, per code

**`malformed_request`** — The client built the request wrongly. Resending it unchanged produces the same 400 for ever, so the batch is quarantined with its reason and sending carries on with the next one. This is a plugin bug and it must be visible as one.

**`unauthorised`** — The events are not the problem, so they are kept. Retrying with a credential the server has just refused cannot succeed and looks exactly like an attack, so sending stops until an operator reactivates the source.

**`source_suspended`** — Distinct from 401 on purpose. The operator's next action is different — a suspended source is resumed, a rejected credential is reactivated — and a plugin that shows one message for both sends the operator down the wrong path.

**`batch_too_large`** — The only failure whose fix is arithmetic. Halve the batch and try again. A single event that is itself too large is an event-level rejection instead, because splitting cannot help it and an event must never be split.

**`rate_limited`** — `Retry-After` is authoritative and overrides any local backoff schedule. A client that backs off less than the server asked for is the reason the server asked.

**`unavailable`** — Nothing was stored. Bounded exponential backoff with jitter — without jitter, every showroom that lost the same deployment returns at the same instant.

**`malformed_event`** — A plugin bug: the event never had the shape the envelope requires. Time does not fix it and neither does a retry, so it is quarantined with the offending field named.

**`schema_unknown`** — Either the plugin is ahead of the registry or the name is wrong. Both need a human, and a quarantined event with the offending name attached is what tells them which.

**`schema_invalid`** — A plugin bug one level deeper than malformed: the envelope is right and the payload is wrong for this event name. Retrying resends the same wrong payload, so it is quarantined.

**`unsupported_version`** — The build is outside the support window. Only an upgrade changes the answer, so the plugin should say so on its diagnostic screen rather than accumulate silently.

**`event_too_large`** — An event is never split. Splitting one would either invent a second event_id — breaking idempotency — or reuse the first, producing two facts from one.

**`reserved_property`** — This is the identity-creep guard. Silently dropping such a key would let a plugin believe for a year that it was setting `project_id`. Rejecting it means somebody finds out on the first run.

**`clock_out_of_range`** — The code exists; the window is OPEN-3 and no policy is proposed here. The reference implementation defaults to accepting and flagging, because a showroom offline longer than an invented bound would otherwise lose its whole backlog to a clock rule rather than to a data problem.

**`pii_suspected`** — LOCKED §5.6: no raw personal data in event properties. The quarantine record stores the offending key and never the offending value — a diagnostic that copies the value has moved the leak rather than stopped it.

**`storage_error`** — The only retryable event-level code, and the only one where the event is fine and the backend is not. Everything else is a property of the event itself.
